INVESTIGATION REPORT
══════════════════════════════════════════════════

═══════════════════════════════════════
INVESTIGATION REPORT — TECHNICAL
═══════════════════════════════════════

REPORT CONFIDENCE:
- Level: LOW (worked out by code from the evidence, not by the AI)
- Why: no knowledge graph for this machine: documents only; only one source found evidence (Alarm)
- Engineer review: NEEDED — confidence is not HIGH


SOURCE DATA:
- DemoBottling-Shift-Log-2026-09-10-Night.csv – three underfill alarms on Filling Line 1, valves 9, 15 and 3 dripping, HIGH confidence.
- DemoBottling-Shift-Log-2026-09-21-Night.csv – low supply pressure note (not a primary cause of current underfill).
- FL-101-Work-Instruction.txt – seal‑kit replacement criteria: replace when a valve drips, when the same valve underfills repeatedly, or when three or more underfill alarms occur in one shift, TIER 2.
- FL-101-Work-Instruction.txt – parts, tools, and safety instructions for seal replacement, TIER 2.

WHAT IS THE ISSUE:
- Root cause: Worn or damaged fill‑valve seals causing valve drip and consequent under‑fill alarms (valves 9, 15, 3). Evidence: shift logs show dripping valves coincident with each alarm; work instruction defines worn seals as the most common cause and mandates seal replacement after three alarms in a shift.
- Difference vs. historical pattern: The current occurrence adds valve 3 to the previously affected valves 9 and 15, indicating the seal‑wear problem is spreading to additional valves.

WHAT IS THE IMPACT:
- Production impact: Line operating at degraded output; bottles are under‑filled, leading to reject count increase and potential line stoppage if alarms persist.
- Safety risk: LOW (no electrical, fire, injury, or foreign‑material events reported).
- Financial impact: Increased reject rate and potential re‑work; exact cost not quantifiable from available data.

HOW CRITICAL IS IT:
- HIGH
- Three under‑fill alarms in a single shift meet the HIGH minimum for recurring faults and trigger the work‑instruction requirement for seal replacement.

HOW TO ADDRESS IT:
- Immediate action:
  Step 1: Safety — LOTO the FL‑101 Bottle Filler, stop production, and isolate the line.
  Step 2: Diagnosis — Inspect fill valves 9, 15, and 3 for dripping between fills; verify seal condition.
  Step 3: Fix — Replace the seal kit on each affected valve using SEAL‑FV‑24 and FGL‑1 lubricant as per FL‑101 work instruction (≈15 min per valve).
  Step 4: Verify — Run a test batch, monitor the checkweigher for under‑fill alarms, and confirm hourly weights are within spec (≈500 ml ± 2 ml).
  Step 5: Quality — Quarantine any bottles produced during the alarm period; perform a visual and weight inspection before release.
- Root cause fix (permanent solution): Replace worn seals on all affected valves and review seal‑replacement interval to prevent recurrence.
- Preventive action: Implement a scheduled seal‑inspection program at 3 months/1 500 running hours; add a daily pre‑start check for valve drip; log any drip immediately for early intervention.
- Who to notify: Maintenance Supervisor (K. Brandt), Production Manager, Quality Assurance Lead.

═══════════════════════════════════════
PLANT MANAGER SUMMARY
═══════════════════════════════════════

SITUATION: Bottles on Filling Line 1 are under‑filled, triggering three alarms in one shift.
ROOT CAUSE: Worn fill‑valve seals on valves 9, 15 and 3 are leaking, causing under‑fill.
STATUS: Line is stopped for LOTO and seal replacement.
ACTION REQUIRED: Replace the seals on the affected valves immediately and restart the line only after verification.
RISK IF NOT ACTIONED: Continued under‑fill will increase rejects, may force an unscheduled line shutdown, and could lead to product compliance issues.

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

Replace the seal kit when:
  - A valve drips between fills
  - The checkweigher shows the same valve underfilling again and again
  - Three or more underfill alarms happen in one shift
  - The seal has reached its limit: 3 months or 1,500 running hours,
    whichever comes first

4. TIME NEEDED

  One valve:                     about 15 minutes
  A typical job (1 to 4 valves): 30 to 45 minutes
  Including rinse and check:     about 1 hour

5. PARTS AND TOOLS

  Seal kit, one per valve:  SEAL-FV-24 (main seal and O-ring)
  Food-grade lubricant:     FGL-1
  Location:                 Filling Line 1 spares cabinet, shelf 2
  Tools:                    valve key, seal pick, clean lint-free cloths,
                            20 empty 500 ml bottles for the check

6. SAFETY

[Source: FL-101-Work-Instruction.txt | Type: Work Instruction | Revision: 1.0 | Score: 0.84]
Step 9 — SANITATION RINSE — MANDATORY
           Run the sanitation rinse for 10 minutes. This removes lubricant
           and any particles from the new seals. Never skip this step: the
           first bottles would carry lubricant into the product.

  Step 10 — FIRST-BOTTLE CHECK — MANDATORY
           Run at normal speed and weigh the first 20 bottles.
           All 20 must be between 495 and 505 ml.
           If any bottle is outside this range, stop and check the valve again.

IMPORTANT: For the first 2 to 3 minutes after a seal change, bottles may be
slightly overfilled (up to 510 ml) while the new seals settle. This is
EXPECTED BEHAVIOUR — not a fault. Do not change any settings. The
checkweigher rejects these bottles automatically.

9. INSPECTING THE OLD SEALS

WHAT IS THE ISSUE:
- Root cause: Wear of fill‑valve seals on valves 9, 15 and newly valve 3 causing drip and underfill, compounded by a low product‑supply pressure event that further reduced fill volume. (Evidence: multiple underfill alarms with dripping valves on 2026‑09‑10; low pressure alarm on 2026‑09‑21; work instruction cites worn seals as most common cause of underfill.)  
- Difference vs historical pattern: Earlier incidents involved only valves 9 and 15; the latest shift shows a third valve (3) also leaking, indicating a spreading seal‑wear issue rather than an isolated valve failure.  

WHAT IS THE IMPACT:
- Production impact: Line stopped for underfill alarms; reduced output while alarms active; potential scrap of underfilled bottles.  
- Safety risk: MEDIUM (no LOTO required by default, but underfill can lead to product quality complaints and downstream rework).  
- Financial impact: Not quantified in data; likely loss from scrap, re‑work, and downtime.

- HIGH – three or more underfill alarms occurred in a single shift (2026‑09‑10) and a low‑pressure alarm required line intervention; recurring fault meets HIGH minimum per rules.  

HOW TO ADDRESS IT:
- Immediate action:
  Step 1: Safety — LOTO the FL‑101 filler, stop production, isolate product supply and air lines.  
  Step 2: Diagnosis — Inspect valves 9, 15 and 3 for seal condition; verify supply pressure and filter status.  
  Step 3: Fix — Replace seal kits on any valve showing drip or underfill (use SEAL‑FV‑24, FGL‑1 lubricant, valve key, seal pick as per work instruction). Clean or replace filter if blocked.  
  Step 4: Verify — Run a test batch, monitor checkweigher for target volume (≈ 500 ml) and confirm no further underfill alarms for at least one full shift.  
  Step 5: Quality — Quarantine any bottles produced during the alarm period; perform weight check and reject underfilled units.

- Preventive action:  
  • Implement a scheduled seal inspection/replacement every 3 months or 1 500 hrs, whichever comes first.  
  • Add a daily pre‑start check for valve drip and supply pressure; log results.  
  • Reinforce filter‑cleaning schedule to avoid low‑pressure events.  
  • Train operators to report any drip immediately; record in shift log.

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

Replace the seal kit when:
  - A valve drips between fills
  - The checkweigher shows the same valve underfilling again and again
  - Three or more underfill alarms happen in one shift
  - The seal has reached its limit: 3 months or 1,500 running hours,
    whichever comes first

4. TIME NEEDED

  One valve:                     about 15 minutes
  A typical job (1 to 4 valves): 30 to 45 minutes
  Including rinse and check:     about 1 hour

5. PARTS AND TOOLS

  Seal kit, one per valve:  SEAL-FV-24 (main seal and O-ring)
  Food-grade lubricant:     FGL-1
  Location:                 Filling Line 1 spares cabinet, shelf 2
  Tools:                    valve key, seal pick, clean lint-free cloths,
                            20 empty 500 ml bottles for the check

6. SAFETY

---

[read by Maintenance Agent · TIER 2 · DOCUMENTS — work instructions]
[Source: FL-101-Work-Instruction.txt | Type: Work Instruction | Revision: 1.0 | Score: 0.82]
8. PROCEDURE

  Step 1 — Press STOP and lock out the machine (LOTO).
  Step 2 — Drain the bowl until the product is below the valve level.
  Step 3 — Remove the valve with the valve key (quarter turn to the left).
  Step 4 — Remove the old seal and O-ring with the seal pick.
  Step 5 — Wipe the valve seat clean with a lint-free cloth. Check it for
           scratches. A scratched seat must be reported to the maintenance
           supervisor: a new seal will not seal on a scratched seat.
  Step 6 — Fit the new seal and O-ring from the SEAL-FV-24 kit, with a thin
           layer of FGL-1 lubricant.
  Step 7 — Refit the valve (quarter turn to the right until it clicks).
  Step 8 — Count the tools and parts on the tray. Remove the lock and refill
           the bowl.

8. PROCEDURE

  Step 1 — Press STOP and lock out the machine (LOTO).

8. PROCEDURE

  Step 1 — Press STOP and lock out the machine (LOTO).
  Step 2 — Drain the bowl until the product is below the valve level.
  Step 3 — Remove the valve with the valve key (quarter turn to the left).
  Step 4 — Remove the old seal and O-ring with the seal pick.
  Step 5 — Wipe the valve seat clean with a lint-free cloth. Check it for
           scratches. A scratched seat must be reported to the maintenance
           supervisor: a new seal will not seal on a scratched seat.
  Step 6 — Fit the new seal and O-ring from the SEAL-FV-24 kit, with a thin
           layer of FGL-1 lubricant.
  Step 7 — Refit the valve (quarter turn to the right until it clicks).
  Step 8 — Count the tools and parts on the tray. Remove the lock and refill
           the bowl.

8. PROCEDURE

  Step 1 — Press STOP and lock out the machine (LOTO).
  Step 2 — Drain the bowl until the product is below the valve level.
  Step 3 — Remove the valve with the valve key (quarter turn to the left).
  Step 4 — Remove the old seal and O-ring with the seal pick.
  Step 5 — Wipe the valve seat clean with a lint-free cloth. Check it for
           scratches. A scratched seat must be reported to the maintenance
           supervisor: a new seal will not seal on a scratched seat.
  Step 6 — Fit the new seal and O-ring from the SEAL-FV-24 kit, with a thin
           layer of FGL-1 lubricant.
  Step 7 — Refit the valve (quarter turn to the right until it clicks).
  Step 8 — Count the tools and parts on the tray. Remove the lock and refill
           the bowl.

- Production impact: Line operating at degraded quality; reject count elevated (14 per 1,000) and bottles under target volume, risking batch hold.
- Safety risk: LOW (no injury, fire, or hazardous material reported); however LOTO required for safe maintenance.

- Preventive action: Implement a valve‑drip monitoring log; schedule seal‑kit replacement proactively before the 3‑month limit; train operators to report any drip immediately; update maintenance planner to generate automatic work order when three underfill alarms occur in a shift.
- Who to notify: Maintenance Supervisor K. Brandt, Shift Supervisor, Quality Assurance Lead, Production Control.

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

Replace the seal kit when:
  - A valve drips between fills
  - The checkweigher shows the same valve underfilling again and again
  - Three or more underfill alarms happen in one shift
  - The seal has reached its limit: 3 months or 1,500 running hours,

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

Replace the seal kit when:
  - A valve drips between fills
  - The checkweigher shows the same valve underfilling again and again
  - Three or more underfill alarms happen in one shift
  - The seal has reached its limit: 3 months or 1,500 running hours,
    whichever comes first

4. TIME NEEDED

  One valve:                     about 15 minutes
  A typical job (1 to 4 valves): 30 to 45 minutes
  Including rinse and check:     about 1 hour

  Food-grade lubricant:     FGL-1
  Location:                 Filling Line 1 spares cabinet, shelf 2
  Tools:                    valve key, seal pick, clean lint-free cloths,
                            20 empty 500 ml bottles for the check

6. SAFETY

2. SCOPE

Applies to all 24 fill valves on the FL-101 Bottle Filler. Only trained
maintenance technicians may carry out this work.

3. WHEN TO REPLACE THE SEALS

Replace the seal kit when:
  - A valve drips between fills
  - The checkweigher shows the same valve underfilling again and again
  - Three or more underfill alarms happen in one shift
  - The seal has reached its limit: 3 months or 1,500 running hours,
    whichever comes first

  One valve:                     about 15 minutes

SOP / PROCEDURE FINDINGS:
- Correct response procedure:  
  1. **Identify the alarm** – “Fill level low — bottles under target volume” (underfill) or “Product supply pressure low — below 1.3 bar”.  
  2. **Immediate action** – Press STOP on the machine.  
  3. **Check product supply pressure** – If the alarm is for low pressure, verify that the pressure is below 1.3 bar.  
  4. **Correct the cause** –  
     - If the supply filter (FLT‑PS‑10) is blocked, clean or replace it.  
     - If air is trapped in the supply line, bleed the air using the bleed valve on the bowl.  
     - If the supply tank is low, check the tank level in the water treatment room.  
  5. **Verify pressure** – Confirm that the pressure has returned to the acceptable range of **1.5 to 2.0 bar**.  
  6. **Restart the line** – After pressure is restored, restart the machine.  
  7. **Re‑weigh bottles** – Weigh the first 20 bottles manually; all must be **495 to 505 ml**.  
  8. **Monitor** – Continue hourly checks of bottle weight and checkweigher reject count; report any increase in rejects to the shift lead.  
- Key specifications:  
  - Target bottle volume: **495 to 505 ml**.  
  - Low product supply pressure alarm threshold: **< 1.3 bar**.  
  - Acceptable pressure range after correction: **1.5 to 2.0 bar**.  
  - Checkweigher reject count: if > 1 bottle in 100 over an hour, report to shift lead.  
- Safety requirements:  
  - Press STOP before performing any maintenance or bleed operations.

SOP / PROCEDURE FINDINGS:
- Correct response procedure:  
  1. **Identify the alarm** – “Fill level low — bottles under target volume” (underfill) or “Product supply pressure low — below 1.3 bar”.  
  2. **Immediate action** – Press STOP on the machine.  
  3. **Check product supply pressure** – If the alarm is for low pressure, verify that the pressure is below 1.3 bar.  
  4. **Correct the cause** –  
     - If the supply filter (FLT‑PS‑10) is blocked, clean or replace it.  
     - If air is trapped in the supply line, bleed the air using the bleed valve on the bowl.  
     - If the supply tank is low, check the tank level in the water treatment room.  
  5. **Verify pressure** – Confirm that the pressure has returned to the acceptable range of **1.5 to 2.0 bar**.  
  6. **Restart the line** – After pressure is restored, restart the machine.  
  7. **Re‑weigh bottles** – Weigh the first 20 bottles manually; all must be **495 to 505 ml**.  
  8. **Monitor** – Continue hourly checks of bottle weight and checkweigher reject count; report any increase in rejects to the shift lead.  
- Key specifications:  
  - Target bottle volume: **495 to 505 ml**.  
  - Low product supply pressure alarm threshold: **< 1.3 bar**.  
  - Acceptable pressure range after correction: **1.5 to 2.0 bar**.  
  - Checkweigher reject count: if > 1 bottle in 100 over an hour, report to shift lead.  
- Safety requirements:  
  - Press STOP before performing any maintenance or bleed operations.  
  - Use appropriate PPE when handling filters or bleeding valves (gloves, eye protection).  
  - Ensure the line is fully stopped and pressure is normalized before restarting.  
- SOP gap: **NO — procedure exists**  
- Data confidence: **HIGH**

FAULT: Underfill  [source: FL-101-SOP Sections 11 and 12.1]
  early warning: If the checkweigher rejects more than 1 bottle in 100 over an hour, tell the shift lead. A rising reject count is often the first sign of worn seals.
  correct response: Press STOP (normal stop, not the emergency stop unless someone is in danger). Dripping valve: call the maintenance technician to replace the seal kit using WI-FL101-001. No dripping: lock out the machine and clean that valve's nozzle. Then check the product supply pressure.
  alarm message: Fill level low — bottles under target volume
  first check: Read the checkweigher report: it shows which valve numbers are underfilling. Look at those valves for dripping.
  causes in order: 1. Worn fill valve seal (the valve drips between fills). 2. Blocked fill nozzle (no dripping). 3. Low product supply pressure (see Product Supply Pressure Low).
  frequency: The most common alarm on FL-101
  alarm trigger: The alarm starts when the checkweigher rejects 3 underfilled bottles in a row
  wrong response: increase the fill time to make up for underfill. It hides worn seals and causes overflow and spillage (NCR-2026-012)
  systemic rule: Three or more underfill alarms in one shift means a systemic fault, usually several worn seals. Stop production, raise a maintenance work order and call the maintenance supervisor.
  definition: A bottle with less than 495 ml
  SPECIFICATION — Fill Volume Specification: allowed range: 495 to 505 ml — the checkweigher rejects anything outside this; hourly check: Every hour, take 5 bottles off the line and weigh them by hand; all must be in range; checkweigher test: Before starting, the 490 ml and 510 ml test bottles must be rejected and the 500 ml bottle must pass. If not, do not start: call the quality lead.; target: 500 ml  [source: FL-101-SOP Sections 8.4, 10 and 11]
  SPECIFICATION — Fill Time Setting: rule: The fill time must NOT be changed by operators. Changing it needs written approval from engineering. A longer fill time does not fix underfill: it hides the real cause and makes bottles overflow.; setting: 3.2 seconds, factory set  [source: FL-101-SOP Section 10]
  Possible causes:
    - Worn Fill Valve Seal  [source: FL-101-SOP Sections 8.1 and 12.1, WI-FL101-001 Sections 3 and 9, NCR-2026-012 Section 5]
        service interval: Every 3 months or 1,500 running hours, whichever comes first
        check: The checkweigher report shows which valves are underfilling. A valve that drips between fills has a worn seal.
        symptom: The valve drips between fills
        signs of wear: Flattened on one side, small cracks at the edge, hard instead of soft, a groove in the sealing face, discoloured or swollen
        ncr reference: NCR-2026-012: seals on valves 7, 12, 13 and 19 were 900 running hours past the 1,500-hour limit
        many worn: If more than 4 seals are badly worn at the same time, tell the maintenance supervisor: the replacement interval may be too long
        part: SEAL-FV-24
            minimum stock: 10 kits
            description: Fill valve seal kit: main seal and O-ring, one per valve
            location: Filling Line 1 spares cabinet, shelf 2
        fix: Fill Valve Seal Replacement  [source: WI-FL101-001 Sections 2 to 8 and 11]
            lubricant rule: Only food-grade lubricant FGL-1. Any other lubricant contaminates the product.
            when to replace: A valve drips between fills; the checkweigher shows the same valve underfilling again and again; three or more underfill alarms in one shift; or the seal has reached 3 months or 1,500 running hours
            before you start: Check the checkweigher report to see which valves are underfilling, mark them with a green tag, and tell the shift lead how long the line will be stopped
            signoff: The shift supervisor signs off the first-bottle check before normal production restarts. Record the date, valve numbers, seal kits used, condition of the old seals, first-bottle results and your name in the maintenance log.
            steps: 1. Press STOP and lock out the machine (LOTO). 2. Drain the bowl until the product is below the valve level. 3. Remove the valve with the valve key (quarter turn to the left). 4. Remove the old seal and O-ring with the seal pick. 5. Wipe the valve seat clean with a lint-free cloth and check it for scratches. 6. Fit the new seal and O-ring from the SEAL-FV-24 kit with a thin layer of FGL-1 lubricant. 7. Refit the valve (quarter turn to the right until it clicks). 8. Count the tools and parts on the tray, remove the lock and refill the bowl. 9. Sanitation rinse (mandatory). 10. First-bottle check (mandatory).
            reference: WI-FL101-001
            important note: For the first 2 to 3 minutes after a seal change, bottles may be slightly overfilled (up to 510 ml) while the new seals settle. This is EXPECTED BEHAVIOUR — not a fault. Do not change any settings.
            scratched seat: A scratched valve seat must be reported to the maintenance supervisor: a new seal will not seal on a scratched seat
            time: One valve about 15 minutes; a typical job (1 to 4 valves) 30 to 45 minutes
            total downtime: about 1 hour including the rinse and the first-bottle check
            who: Trained maintenance technicians only
            then required: Sanitation Rinse  [source: WI-FL101-001 Step 9, FL-101-SOP Sections 4, 9, 12.3 and 17]
                method: Rinse the bowl, valves and nozzles with clean water for 10 minutes. This removes lubricant and particles from the new seals.
                also required: At start-up if the machine has been stopped for more than 4 hours, after glass breakage, and at the end of every shift
                mandatory: true — never skip it after a seal change: the first bottles would carry lubricant into the product
            then required: First-Bottle Check  [source: WI-FL101-001 Step 10 and Section 11]
                method: Run at normal speed and weigh the first 20 bottles. All 20 must be between 495 and 505 ml. If any bottle is outside this range, stop and check the valve again.
                signoff: The shift supervisor signs off the first-bottle check
                mandatory: true — normal production must not restart without it
            then required: LOTO (SAF-003)  [source: FL-101-SOP Section 6.2]
                lock rule: Only the person who fitted a lock may remove it
                required before: Any maintenance, clearing a jam, changing parts, or reaching into the machine
                steps: 1. Switch off power at the main isolator. 2. Lock the isolator with your personal padlock. 3. Tag it with your name and the date. 4. Try to start the machine to prove it cannot run.
        known pattern: Fill Time Trap  [source: NCR-2026-012 Sections 5 and 8]
            chain: Worn seals drip → underfill alarms → fill time raised 3.2 → 3.6 → 3.9 s → most valves overflow → spillage and wet labels → 1,200 bottles rejected, 2 hours 10 minutes downtime
            correct response: Underfill is a seal problem until proven otherwise: check for dripping valves first and replace worn seals (WI-FL101-001). Leave the fill time at the factory setting.
            wrong response: raise the fill time to fix underfill
            description: The operator raises the fill time to make up for underfill caused by worn seals, and most valves then overflow
            lesson from: NCR-2026-012, night shift of 16 January 2026
    - Blocked Fill Nozzle  [source: FL-101-SOP Section 12.1, WI-FL101-001 Section 10]
        symptom: The valve underfills but does not drip: debris in the nozzle
        fix: Fill Nozzle Cleaning  [source: FL-101-SOP Section 12.1 Step 4, WI-FL101-001 Section 10]
            method: Lock out the machine and clean the nozzle of the underfilling valve
            then required: LOTO (SAF-003) (details above)

Bottles on QA HOLD may only be released after the quality lead has
inspected them.

12.4 Product Supply Pressure Low
Alarm message: "Product supply pressure low — below 1.3 bar"

Low supply pressure makes bottles underfill.

Causes, most common first:
  1. Supply filter blocked — clean or replace the filter (FLT-PS-10)
  2. Air in the supply line — bleed the air using the bleed valve on the bowl
  3. Supply tank running low — check the tank level with the water
     treatment room

Immediate action:
  Step 1 — Press STOP.
  Step 2 — Clean the supply filter.
  Step 3 — Bleed air from the supply line.
  Step 4 — Confirm the pressure is back to 1.5 to 2.0 bar.
  Step 5 — Restart, then weigh the first 20 bottles. All must be 495 to 505 ml.

12.4 Product Supply Pressure Low
Alarm message: "Product supply pressure low — below 1.3 bar"

Low supply pressure makes bottles underfill.

Causes, most common first:
  1. Supply filter blocked — clean or replace the filter (FLT-PS-10)
  2. Air in the supply line — bleed the air using the bleed valve on the bowl
  3. Supply tank running low — check the tank level with the water
     treatment room

Immediate action:
  Step 1 — Press STOP.
  Step 2 — Clean the supply filter.
  Step 3 — Bleed air from the supply line.
  Step 4 — Confirm the pressure is back to 1.5 to 2.0 bar.
  Step 5 — Restart, then weigh the first 20 bottles. All must be 495 to 505 ml.

The alarm starts when the checkweigher rejects 3 underfilled bottles in a row.

12.4 Product Supply Pressure Low
Alarm message: "Product supply pressure low — below 1.3 bar"

Low supply pressure makes bottles underfill.

Causes, most common first:
  1. Supply filter blocked — clean or replace the filter (FLT-PS-10)
  2. Air in the supply line — bleed the air using the bleed valve on the bowl
  3. Supply tank running low — check the tank level with the water
     treatment room

  • Low product supply pressure alarm threshold: < 1.3 bar.

graph_text:
KNOWLEDGE GRAPH FOR FL-101 — human-reviewed facts, each with its source.

FAULT: Underfill  [source: FL-101-SOP Sections 11 and 12.1]
  early warning: If the checkweigher rejects more than 1 bottle in 100 over an hour, tell the shift lead. A rising reject count is often the first sign of worn seals.
  correct response: Press STOP (normal stop, not the emergency stop unless someone is in danger). Dripping valve: call the maintenance technician to replace the seal kit using WI-FL101-001. No dripping: lock out the machine and clean that valve's nozzle. Then check the product supply pressure.
  alarm message: Fill level low — bottles under target volume
  first check: Read the checkweigher report: it shows which valve numbers are underfilling. Look at those valves for dripping.
  causes in order: 1. Worn fill valve seal (the valve drips between fills). 2. Blocked fill nozzle (no dripping). 3. Low product supply pressure (see Product Supply Pressure Low).
  frequency: The most common alarm on FL-101
  alarm trigger: The alarm starts when the checkweigher rejects 3 underfilled bottles in a row
  wrong response: increase the fill time to make up for underfill. It hides worn seals and causes overflow and spillage (NCR-2026-012)
  systemic rule: Three or more underfill alarms in one shift means a systemic fault, usually several worn seals. Stop production, raise a maintenance work order and call the maintenance supervisor.
  definition: A bottle with less than 495 ml
  SPECIFICATION — Fill Volume Specification: allowed range: 495 to 505 ml — the checkweigher rejects anything outside this; hourly check: Every hour, take 5 bottles off the line and weigh them by hand; all must be in range; checkweigher test: Before starting, the 490 ml and 510 ml test bottles must be rejected and the 500 ml bottle must pass. If not, do not start: call the quality lead.; target: 500 ml  [source: FL-101-SOP Sections 8.4, 10 and 11]
  SPECIFICATION — Fill Time Setting: rule: The fill time must NOT be changed by operators. Changing it needs written approval from engineering. A longer fill time does not fix underfill: it hides the real cause and makes bottles overflow.; setting: 3.2 seconds, factory set  [source: FL-101-SOP Section 10]
  Possible causes:
    - Worn Fill Valve Seal  [source: FL-101-SOP Sections 8.1 and 12.1, WI-FL101-001 Sections 3 and 9, NCR-2026-012 Section 5]
        service interval: Every 3 months or 1,500 running hours, whichever comes first
        check: The checkweigher report shows which valves are underfilling. A valve that drips between fills has a worn seal.
        symptom: The valve drips between fills
        signs of wear: Flattened on one side, small cracks at the edge, hard instead of soft, a groove in the sealing face, discoloured or swollen
        ncr reference: NCR-2026-012: seals on valves 7, 12, 13 and 19 were 900 running hours past the 1,500-hour limit
        many worn: If more than 4 seals are badly worn at the same time, tell the maintenance supervisor: the replacement interval may be too long
        part: SEAL-FV-24
            minimum stock: 10 kits
            description: Fill valve seal kit: main seal and O-ring, one per valve
            location: Filling Line 1 spares cabinet, shelf 2
        fix: Fill Valve Seal Replacement  [source: WI-FL101-001 Sections 2 to 8 and 11]
            lubricant rule: Only food-grade lubricant FGL-1. Any other lubricant contaminates the product.
            when to replace: A valve drips between fills; the checkweigher shows the same valve underfilling again and again; three or more underfill alarms in one shift; or the seal has reached 3 months or 1,500 running hours
            before you start: Check the checkweigher report to see which valves are underfilling, mark them with a green tag, and tell the shift lead how long the line will be stopped
            signoff: The shift supervisor signs off the first-bottle check before normal production restarts. Record the date, valve numbers, seal kits used, condition of the old seals, first-bottle results and your name in the maintenance log.
            steps: 1. Press STOP and lock out the machine (LOTO). 2. Drain the bowl until the product is below the valve level. 3. Remove the valve with the valve key (quarter turn to the left). 4. Remove the old seal and O-ring with the seal pick. 5. Wipe the valve seat clean with a lint-free cloth and check it for scratches. 6. Fit the new seal and O-ring from the SEAL-FV-24 kit with a thin layer of FGL-1 lubricant. 7. Refit the valve (quarter turn to the right until it clicks). 8. Count the tools and parts on the tray, remove the lock and refill the bowl. 9. Sanitation rinse (mandatory). 10. First-bottle check (mandatory).
            reference: WI-FL101-001
            important note: For the first 2 to 3 minutes after a seal change, bottles may be slightly overfilled (up to 510 ml) while the new seals settle. This is EXPECTED BEHAVIOUR — not a fault. Do not change any settings.
            scratched seat: A scratched valve seat must be reported to the maintenance supervisor: a new seal will not seal on a scratched seat
            time: One valve about 15 minutes; a typical job (1 to 4 valves) 30 to 45 minutes
            total downtime: about 1 hour including the rinse and the first-bottle check
            who: Trained maintenance technicians only
            then required: Sanitation Rinse  [source: WI-FL101-001 Step 9, FL-101-SOP Sections 4, 9, 12.3 and 17]
                method: Rinse the bowl, valves and nozzles with clean water for 10 minutes. This removes lubricant and particles from the new seals.
                also required: At start-up if the machine has been stopped for more than 4 hours, after glass breakage, and at the end of every shift
                mandatory: true — never skip it after a seal change: the first bottles would carry lubricant into the product
            then required: First-Bottle Check  [source: WI-FL101-001 Step 10 and Section 11]
                method: Run at normal speed and weigh the first 20 bottles. All 20 must be between 495 and 505 ml. If any bottle is outside this range, stop and check the valve again.
                signoff: The shift supervisor signs off the first-bottle check
                mandatory: true — normal production must not restart without it
            then required: LOTO (SAF-003)  [source: FL-101-SOP Section 6.2]
                lock rule: Only the person who fitted a lock may remove it
                required before: Any maintenance, clearing a jam, changing parts, or reaching into the machine
                steps: 1. Switch off power at the main isolator. 2. Lock the isolator with your personal padlock. 3. Tag it with your name and the date. 4. Try to start the machine to prove it cannot run.
        known pattern: Fill Time Trap  [source: NCR-2026-012 Sections 5 and 8]
            chain: Worn seals drip → underfill alarms → fill time raised 3.2 → 3.6 → 3.9 s → most valves overflow → spillage and wet labels → 1,200 bottles rejected, 2 hours 10 minutes downtime
            correct response: Underfill is a seal problem until proven otherwise: check for dripping valves first and replace worn seals (WI-FL101-001). Leave the fill time at the factory setting.
            wrong response: raise the fill time to fix underfill
            description: The operator raises the fill time to make up for underfill caused by worn seals, and most valves then overflow
            lesson from: NCR-2026-012, night shift of 16 January 2026
    - Blocked Fill Nozzle  [source: FL-101-SOP Section 12.1, WI-FL101-001 Section 10]
        symptom: The valve underfills but does not drip: debris in the nozzle
        fix: Fill Nozzle Cleaning  [source: FL-101-SOP Section 12.1 Step 4, WI-FL101-001 Section 10]
            method: Lock out the machine and clean the nozzle of the underfilling valve
            then required: LOTO (SAF-003) (details above)
  pattern: Fill Time Trap (details above)
  pattern: Systemic Underfill Indicator  [source: FL-101-SOP Sections 12.1 and 13, NCR-2026-012 Section 8]
      correct response: Stop production, raise a maintenance work order and call the maintenance supervisor
      meaning: Several worn seals: a systemic fault, not bad luck
      trigger: 3 or more underfill alarms in one shift
      then required: Fill Valve Seal Replacement (details above)
      then required: Escalate to Maintenance Supervisor  [source: FL-101-SOP Section 13]
          electrical rule: Do not attempt electrical repairs. Always call maintenance.

          trigger 4: A guide rail will not lock in position
          trigger 5: Any glass breakage (also call the quality lead)

Machine-wide safety (applies to any work on this machine):
  LOTO (SAF-003) (details above)
  PPE Required on Filling Line 1  [source: FL-101-SOP Section 6.1]
      feet: Safety shoes
      hands: Cut-resistant gloves when handling glass or change parts
      hearing: Hearing protection
      eyes: Safety glasses at all times
  Machine Safety Rules  [source: FL-101-SOP Sections 6.3 and 6.4]
      air rule: Never use compressed air near open bottles or broken glass

- Production impact: Line operating at degraded rate; high reject count forces frequent stops for bottle removal and quality checks; estimated downtime ~1 hour for seal replacement and required rinses.
- Safety risk: MEDIUM – maintenance requires LOTO and PPE; no immediate injury but improper work could create hazards.
- Financial impact: Lost production time (~1 hour) plus cost of seal kits (SEAL‑FV‑24) and labor; increased reject waste.

- HIGH – three or more underfill alarms in one shift meet the systemic fault rule; requires immediate stop and maintenance work order.

Immediate action (follow SOP and WI‑FL101‑001):

Step 3: Fix — For each dripping valve:
  1. Drain the bowl below valve level.
  2. Remove the valve with the valve key.
  3. Remove old seal and O‑ring; inspect seat for scratches.
  4. Install new SEAL‑FV‑24 kit seal and O‑ring with a thin layer of food‑grade lubricant FGL‑1.
  5. Re‑fit valve, remove lock, refill bowl.
  6. Perform mandatory sanitation rinse (10 min clean water).
Step 4: Verify — Run first‑bottle check: weigh first 20 bottles; all must be 495‑505 ml. If any out of range, repeat seal inspection.
Step 5: Quality — Record seal replacement details (valve numbers, part numbers, technician name) in maintenance log; quarantine any bottles produced before successful first‑bottle check.

- Replace all worn fill‑valve seals on the line and enforce the 3‑month / 1,500 hour replacement interval; update maintenance schedule to include pre‑emptive seal inspection after 1,200 hours.

Preventive action:
- Add a daily check of valve drip condition to the shift checklist.
- Configure the checkweigher alarm to trigger a maintenance work order after two underfill alarms (early warning).
- Train operators to report any valve drip immediately; reinforce “do NOT increase fill time” rule.
- Review seal inventory to ensure minimum stock of 10 kits is maintained.

- Shift supervisor (immediate stop and LOTO)
- Maintenance supervisor (work order for seal replacement)
- Quality lead (record NCR closure and first‑bottle verification)

The alarm starts when the checkweigher rejects 3 underfilled bottles in a row.

This is the most common alarm on FL-101. Causes, most common first:

Alarm message: "Product supply pressure low — below 1.3 bar"

Low supply pressure makes bottles underfill.

Causes, most common first:
  1. Supply filter blocked — clean or replace the filter (FLT-PS-10)
  2. Air in the supply line — bleed the air using the bleed valve on the bowl
  3. Supply tank running low — check the tank level with the water
     treatment room

Immediate action:
  Step 1 — Press STOP.
  Step 2 — Clean the supply filter.
  Step 3 — Bleed air from the supply line.
  Step 4 — Confirm the pressure is back to 1.5 to 2.0 bar.

     - Step 1: Press STOP.  
     - Step 2: Clean or replace the supply filter (FLT‑PS‑10).  
     - Step 3: Bleed air from the supply line using the bleed valve on the bowl.  
     - Step 4: Confirm pressure is back to 1.5–2.0 bar (alarm threshold is 1.3 bar).  
     - Step 5: Restart the line.  
     - Step 6: Weigh the first 20 bottles; all must be 495–505 ml.  
  4. **If no low pressure** – inspect valves/nozzles as above and correct any mechanical issue.  
  5. **After correction** – resume normal operation and monitor checkweigher reject count.  

- Key specifications:  
  - Target bottle volume: **495–505 ml**.  
  - Product supply pressure alarm threshold: **< 1.3 bar**.  
  - Acceptable pressure after correction: **1.5–2.0 bar**.  
  - Checkweigher reject count: if > 1 bottle in 100 per hour, report to shift lead.  

- Safety requirements:  
  - Press STOP before performing any maintenance on the fill line.  
  - Use appropriate PPE when handling valves, filters, and bleed valves (gloves, eye protection).  
  - Ensure the line is fully stopped and pressure is within safe limits before opening any valves.  

- SOP gap: **NO — procedure exists**.  

- Data confidence: **HIGH**.  

SOURCES USED:
- FL‑101‑SOP.txt (Revision 1.0) – sections 12.1 (Underfill), 12.4 (Product Supply Pressure Low), 11 (Checks During the Shift).

KNOWLEDGE GRAPH FOR FL-101 — human-reviewed facts, each with its source.

FAULT: Underfill  [source: FL-101-SOP Sections 11 and 12.1]
  early warning: If the checkweigher rejects more than 1 bottle in 100 over an hour, tell the shift lead. A rising reject count is often the first sign of worn seals.
  correct response: Press STOP (normal stop, not the emergency stop unless someone is in danger). Dripping valve: call the maintenance technician to replace the seal kit using WI-FL101-001. No dripping: lock out the machine and clean that valve's nozzle. Then check the product supply pressure.
  alarm message: Fill level low — bottles under target volume
  first check: Read the checkweigher report: it shows which valve numbers are underfilling. Look at those valves for dripping.
  causes in order: 1. Worn fill valve seal (the valve drips between fills). 2. Blocked fill nozzle (no dripping). 3. Low product supply pressure (see Product Supply Pressure Low).
  frequency: The most common alarm on FL-101
  alarm trigger: The alarm starts when the checkweigher rejects 3 underfilled bottles in a row
  wrong response: increase the fill time to make up for underfill. It hides worn seals and causes overflow and spillage (NCR-2026-012)
  systemic rule: Three or more underfill alarms in one shift means a systemic fault, usually several worn seals. Stop production, raise a maintenance work order and call the maintenance supervisor.
  definition: A bottle with less than 495 ml
  SPECIFICATION — Fill Volume Specification: allowed range: 495 to 505 ml — the checkweigher rejects anything outside this; hourly check: Every hour, take 5 bottles off the line and weigh them by hand; all must be in range; checkweigher test: Before starting, the 490 ml and 510 ml test bottles must be rejected and the 500 ml bottle must pass. If not, do not start: call the quality lead.; target: 500 ml  [source: FL-101-SOP Sections 8.4, 10 and 11]
  SPECIFICATION — Fill Time Setting: rule: The fill time must NOT be changed by operators. Changing it needs written approval from engineering. A longer fill time does not fix underfill: it hides the real cause and makes bottles overflow.; setting: 3.2 seconds, factory set  [source: FL-101-SOP Section 10]
  Possible causes:
    - Worn Fill Valve Seal  [source: FL-101-SOP Sections 8.1 and 12.1, WI-FL101-001 Sections 3 and 9, NCR-2026-012 Section 5]
        service interval: Every 3 months or 1,500 running hours, whichever comes first
        check: The checkweigher report shows which valves are underfilling. A valve that drips between fills has a worn seal.
        symptom: The valve drips between fills
        signs of wear: Flattened on one side, small cracks at the edge, hard instead of soft, a groove in the sealing face, discoloured or swollen
        ncr reference: NCR-2026-012: seals on valves 7, 12, 13 and 19 were 900 running hours past the 1,500-hour limit
        many worn: If more than 4 seals are badly worn at the same time, tell the maintenance supervisor: the replacement interval may be too long
        part: SEAL-FV-24
            minimum stock: 10 kits
            description: Fill valve seal kit: main seal and O-ring, one per valve
            location: Filling Line 1 spares cabinet, shelf 2
        fix: Fill Valve Seal Replacement  [source: WI-FL101-001 Sections 2 to 8 and 11]
            lubricant rule: Only food-grade lubricant FGL-1. Any other lubricant contaminates the product.
            when to replace: A valve drips between fills; the checkweigher shows the same valve underfilling again and again; three or more underfill alarms in one shift; or the seal has reached 3 months or 1,500 running hours
            before you start: Check the checkweigher report to see which valves are underfilling, mark them with a green tag, and tell the shift lead how long the line will be stopped
            signoff: The shift supervisor signs off the first-bottle check before normal production restarts. Record the date, valve numbers, seal kits used, condition of the old seals, first-bottle results and your name in the maintenance log.
            steps: 1. Press STOP and lock out the machine (LOTO). 2. Drain the bowl until the product is below the valve level. 3. Remove the valve with the valve key (quarter turn to the left). 4. Remove the old seal and O-ring with the seal pick. 5. Wipe the valve seat clean with a lint-free cloth and check it for scratches. 6. Fit the new seal and O-ring from the SEAL-FV-24 kit with a thin layer of FGL-1 lubricant. 7. Refit the valve (quarter turn to the right until it clicks). 8. Count the tools and parts on the tray, remove the lock and refill the bowl. 9. Sanitation rinse (mandatory). 10. First-bottle check (mandatory).
            reference: WI-FL101-001
            important note: For the first 2 to 3 minutes after a seal change, bottles may be slightly overfilled (up to 510 ml) while the new seals settle. This is EXPECTED BEHAVIOUR — not a fault. Do not change any settings.
            scratched seat: A scratched valve seat must be reported to the maintenance supervisor: a new seal will not seal on a scratched seat
            time: One valve about 15 minutes; a typical job (1 to 4 valves) 30 to 45 minutes
            total downtime: about 1 hour including the rinse and the first-bottle check
            who: Trained maintenance technicians only
            then required: Sanitation Rinse  [source: WI-FL101-001 Step 9, FL-101-SOP Sections 4, 9, 12.3 and 17]
                method: Rinse the bowl, valves and nozzles with clean water for 10 minutes. This removes lubricant and particles from the new seals.
                also required: At start-up if the machine has been stopped for more than 4 hours, after glass breakage, and at the end of every shift
                mandatory: true — never skip it after a seal change: the first bottles would carry lubricant into the product
            then required: First-Bottle Check  [source: WI-FL101-001 Step 10 and Section 11]
                method: Run at normal speed and weigh the first 20 bottles. All 20 must be between 495 and 505 ml. If any bottle is outside this range, stop and check the valve again.
                signoff: The shift supervisor signs off the first-bottle check
                mandatory: true — normal production must not restart without it
            then required: LOTO (SAF-003)  [source: FL-101-SOP Section 6.2]
                lock rule: Only the person who fitted a lock may remove it
                required before: Any maintenance, clearing a jam, changing parts, or reaching into the machine
                steps: 1. Switch off power at the main isolator. 2. Lock the isolator with your personal padlock. 3. Tag it with your name and the date. 4. Try to start the machine to prove it cannot run.
        known pattern: Fill Time Trap  [source: NCR-2026-012 Sections 5 and 8]
            chain: Worn seals drip → underfill alarms → fill time raised 3.2 → 3.6 → 3.9 s → most valves overflow → spillage and wet labels → 1,200 bottles rejected, 2 hours 10 minutes downtime
            correct response: Underfill is a seal problem until proven otherwise: check for dripping valves first and replace worn seals (WI-FL101-001). Leave the fill time at the factory setting.
            wrong response: raise the fill time to fix underfill
            description: The operator raises the fill time to make up for underfill caused by worn seals, and most valves then overflow
            lesson from: NCR-2026-012, night shift of 16 January 2026
    - Blocked Fill Nozzle  [source: FL-101-SOP Section 12.1, WI-FL101-001 Section 10]
        symptom: The valve underfills but does not drip: debris in the nozzle
        fix: Fill Nozzle Cleaning  [source: FL-101-SOP Section 12.1 Step 4, WI-FL101-001 Section 10]
            method: Lock out the machine and clean the nozzle of the underfilling valve
            then required: LOTO (SAF-003) (details above)
  pattern: Fill Time Trap (details above)
  pattern: Systemic Underfill Indicator  [source: FL-101-SOP Sections 12.1 and 13, NCR-2026-012 Section 8]
      correct response: Stop production, raise a maintenance work order and call the maintenance supervisor
